title: The 25 Best Central Midfielders in World Soccer—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By SI FC StaffJul 20, 2025Pedri often runs the show for Barça.  / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesTrying to define a “central midfielder” in modern soccer is no simple task.

With positions more fluid than ever and tactical roles constantly evolving, midfielders today are asked to do a bit of everything—defend, build play, break lines, press and even score. But amid all this complexity, there’s still a distinction between the different types of midfielders.

This list focuses exclusively on true central midfielders—those who typically operate in the No. 8 role or as balanced, box-to-box players. These are the players who connect defence and attack, carry the ball through midfield, and often dictate the rhythm of a match from the centre of the park.

To keep things clear, we've excluded traditional defensive midfielders (the out-and-out No. 6s), as well as classic attacking midfielders (the No. 10s) who play higher up the pitch in more advanced creative roles. Both of those categories deserve separate recognition.

What remains is a group of versatile, influential midfielders who embody the modern game's demands. And while ranking them is no easy feat, here’s Sports Illustrated's carefully considered list of the current 25 best.

André-Frank Zambo Anguissa has won Serie A twice with Napoli. / Timothy Rogers/Getty ImagesFulham fans will remember André-Frank Zambo Anguissa as the midfield mountain who flashed glimpses of brilliance but, strangely given his size and strength, struggled to fully adapt to the Premier League.In Naples, though, Anguissa has become a force of nature. A two-time Serie A champion, Anguissa has been the beating heart of one of the most glorious chapters in Napoli’s history. Commanding the midfield with a lethal mix of defensive savvy and explosive ball-carrying power, he’s evolved into a true game-changer.

Mateo Kovačić has struggled with injury. / Alex Livesey/Danehouse/Getty ImagesMateo Kovačić’s résumé speaks for itself—Inter, Real Madrid, Chelsea, Manchester City—a glittering list that stands as a testament to his elite pedigree.The Croatian maestro is one of the game’s most gifted ball-progressing midfielders, capable of slicing through defensive lines with pinpoint vertical passes—the kind that have become a rare commodity in an age dominated by safe, sideways soccer.While injuries have hampered him at City, Kovačić rises to the occasion whenever he's fit, often chipping in with crucial goals, too.

Thuram is a key player for Juventus. / Juventus FC/Getty ImagesKhéphren Thuram comes from soccer royalty—the son of French legend Lilian Thuram and younger brother of Inter forward Marcus Thuram. Now with a star of his own firmly on the rise, the youngest Thuram is doing the family name proud.The towering midfielder has been one of the few bright spots during a difficult couple of seasons for Juventus, with his dynamic, all-action displays quickly turning heads. His blend of physicality, press resistance and powerful line-breaking runs gave Juve some much-needed energy and drive through the middle of the pitch.Add in growing consistency, maturity and defensive steel, and Thuram’s inclusion in the Serie A Team of the Season for 2024–25 merely confirmed what many had already suspected: he’s is the real deal.

Youri Tielemans has boosted United’s midfield. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesAs a free transfer, Youri Tielemans was a signing of extraordinary value for an Aston Villa side doing things their fans could only have dreamed of a decade earlier, when the club was staring down the barrel of Premier League relegation. In the middle of the pitch, the Belgian did just about everything for the Villans, combining accomplished passing with a willingness to shoot from distance and a tenacious edge when it came to winning the ball back.Comparisons with fellow Belgian and Premier League legend Kevin De Bruyne were made, while Villa boss Unai Emery even said he saw Tielemans like his “son”—a particularly bizarre choice of words given that the pair once had a physical confrontation.Sadly for Villa fans, after helping establish the club as a top-four force and leading them to Europa League glory in 2025–26, Tielemans followed several of Villa’s other stars out the door this summer, joining Manchester United. For United, though, adding a midfielder with his technical quality and intelligence could prove a very shrewd piece of business.

Felix Nmecha is a two-way force. / Ralf Ibing/firo sportphoto/Getty ImagesFelix Nmecha was never really given his chance by either Manchester City or England, despite representing both at youth level, with his senior opportunities limited to a handful of cup cameos for City.Their loss has been Borussia Dortmund’s and Germany’s gain, however, with the towering 6'3" midfielder now a regular for both club and country, proving just how wrong his former employers were to let him go.A colossal ball carrier and superb passer, Nmecha also has a knack for chipping in with crucial goals and assists, making him an increasingly complete presence in the middle of the pitch.

Goretzka is now a Villan. / Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty ImagesLeon Goretzka’s journey from lean and lanky to relentless powerhouse at Bayern Munich saw him evolve into one of the world’s most fearsome midfield forces.He might not dazzle with silky skills, but what he lacks in finesse, the now-Aston Villa star more than makes up for with sheer effectiveness. His timing when bursting into the box is impeccable and, off the ball, he covers ground like a machine that never quits.While he may have lost a bit of the raw power that once defined him, when Goretzka is on form, there’s no denying his class.

Pablo Barrios is a regular under Diego Simeone. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIn the eyes of Diego Simeone, Pablo Barrios’s performances in Atlético Madrid’s midfield “speak for themselves.”“He gives us energy, a good pace of play, he applies pressure,” the Argentine coach gushed of the Spain international last season. “He gives us direction and security in that area of the midfield where we need legs. He’s doing it in the best way possible, he’s growing year after year.”The natural heir to Koke is not one for flashy goals or assists tallies. The beauty of Barrios’s game lies in its subtlety and spirit.

Mainoo remains indispensable in Man Utd’s midfield. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesThere’s no denying that Kobbie Mainoo has endured a tough year or so. Frozen out by Rúben Amorim, his Manchester United career looked to be over, with his rapid rise from promising youngster to one of world soccer’s finest young talents seemingly grinding to a halt.Then came his older brother, the “Free Kobbie Mainoo” T-shirt, the appointment of Michael Carrick and a renewed vote of confidence in the young Englishman—and suddenly, Mainoo looks right back on track.One of the most technically gifted players at United—and in England’s squad—Mainoo is superbly composed on the ball, capable of threading line-breaking passes through the tightest spaces, while remaining dogged and tenacious without it. He’s the full package, and despite United’s heavy summer investment in midfield, Mainoo remains indispensable.

Adrien Rabiot has undergone one hell of a career arc. / Antonino Lagana/Getty ImagesFor a player who won five Ligue 1 titles with an all-conquering Paris Saint-Germain side in the 2010s, it might seem strange to say that Adrien Rabiot is only now hitting his prime—especially now he’s in his thirties and has left Marseille for AC Milan.But that’s exactly what’s happened.First at Juventus, and now back in Serie A at San Siro, Rabiot has evolved from a graceful, dependable midfielder into a genuine match-winner. He’s added bite, goals, and a cutting edge to his game—becoming far more than just a composed presence in the middle of the park.Between 2022–23 and 2025–26, the France international netted more goals than managed in the entire rest of his career, which began way back in 2011. It’s a remarkable transformation and proof that Rabiot has rewritten the final chapters of his career on his own terms—not fading away, but stepping up.

Ederson almost moved to the Premier League. / Elianton/Mondadori Portfolio/Getty ImagesJust a few years ago, Ederson (the Brazilian midfielder, not the goalkeeper) was struggling for minutes with relegation-threatened Salernitana. Now, he’s one of the most complete midfielders in Europe—a Brazil international, a European champion and the beating heart of a resurgent Atalanta.His meteoric rise has mirrored that of his club. As Atalanta transformed from Serie A staples into genuine title contenders and Europa League winners, Ederson was at the center of it all. A tireless engine who covers ground like few others, he presses aggressively, wins duels, and gives his more attack-minded teammates the freedom to shine.But don’t be fooled into thinking he’s just a destroyer. Ederson is excellent on the ball, too—a smooth, purposeful carrier and a tidy passer.

Gavi is currently locked in a battle for minutes at Barcelona. / Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesWhen fit and injury-free—which has too often been an issue during Gavi’s fledgling career—the diminutive Spaniard brings an intensity few can match, combining tireless running and fearless tackling with the kind of technical finesse that sets him apart.His sharp close control, quick turns in tight spaces and ability to find a pass under pressure offer flashes of the great Andrés Iniesta, yet Gavi plays with a snarl and bite that are entirely his own. He doesn’t just play the game; he throws himself into it, fully and relentlessly, every single time.Unfortunately, that all-action style has seemingly gone hand in hand with his growing injury record, with Gavi’s willingness to put his body on the line perhaps contributing to a career that has too often been interrupted. But there’s little doubt that when he is fit and available, Barcelona are a better team with Gavi in it.

Alexis Mac Allister is still integral for Liverpool. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesIn 2022, Alexis Mac Allister was quietly making his mark at Brighton—a talented midfielder, but one still flying somewhat under the radar.Then came the World Cup. Alongside Lionel Messi, Mac Allister suddenly had the world watching, and Argentina’s triumphant run provided a perfect showcase of just how special he really was. The pair developed an almost telepathic understanding, constantly seeking each other out and seeming to speak the same soccer language without saying a word.That alone should tell you plenty about Mac Allister’s quality, yet even now, as a World Cup winner and Premier League champion with Liverpool, his modest, unassuming personality means he can still be underestimated.The quintessential modern box-to-box midfielder, Mac Allister excels in almost every department, whether it’s tenacious tackling, relentless ball-winning, dominating duels, precise passing or long-range shooting.

Luka Modrić left Real Madrid in 2025. / Timothy Rogers/Getty ImagesAbility-wise, Luka Modrić is still right up there with the best—his vision, technique, and intelligence remain as sharp as ever. But even the greats can’t outrun time.Though he may not have the engine he once did, make no mistake—Modrić can still outthink, out-pass and outplay most midfielders in the game. His control of tempo, exquisite range of passing and eye for a killer ball remain untouched. He can unlock a defence in an instant and still strike fear with a fierce shot from distance.Even in the twilight of his career, Modrić—now with AC Milan—isn't fading, he’s simply adapting.

Expectations for Elliot Anderson are high at City. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesWith less than 12 months to go until the 2026 World Cup, Elliot Anderson had never received a senior international call-up. By the time the tournament arrived, he was one of the first names on England’s team sheet.Those at Newcastle United had seen Anderson’s talent up close for themselves. The proud Geordie came through the club’s academy before moving to Nottingham Forest in the summer of 2024, where two stellar seasons turned him into one of the Premier League’s most sought-after midfielders. Manchester City eventually paid £116 million ($156 million) for his services, bringing him to the Etihad as part of their post-Pep Guardiola rebuild.An elite ball-winner with a relentless pressing game and progressive passing ability, Anderson looks perfectly suited to become a heartbeat of Manchester City’s next era.
